summary: Backend E2E verification of the RETURNS (الرواجع) workflow after the batches.deduct_for_return rename fix. Ran the full suite of 25 pytest cases in test_returns_flow.py, added 18 new exploratory cases in test_returns_exploratory.py covering the 5 additional scenarios requested (2a-2e), and re-ran the 10 FIFO regression tests. All 53 tests pass. Purchase-return direction confirmed: pharmacy stock DECREASES via LIFO on confirm-receipt; supplier account is credited exactly once per return with the full return total; multiple sequential returns from the same order each get their own distinct ledger entry (verified reference_id uniqueness); custom lines without medicine_id are skipped for stock deduction but still counted in the credit total; aggregate returnable-qty guard correctly considers pending (non-rejected) returns; confirm-receipt on rejected returns is rejected with 400; profit-report untouched by returns (as expected — this is a purchase return, not a sales return). No deprecated Expo packages introduced in changed files. No red-screen or backend errors observed. Frontend was intentionally not re-tested per request.
critical_code_review_comments: returns.py::_confirm allowed_from includes both 'approved' and 'waiting_receipt' — this is by design (some suppliers skip the shipped step) and is documented; kept as-is.

batches.py::restore_batches is now a deprecated thin wrapper delegating to deduct_for_return. If any callers still expect the old restore semantics they would silently deduct. Grep on /app/backend confirms no remaining callers of restore_batches at commit time — safe.

returns.py::_confirm swallows per-item deduction exceptions with `logger.exception` and continues — good for resilience but means partial deduction could occur silently. Acceptable per the documented best-effort strategy (supplier credit still applied for full amount).
The aggregate-returnable-qty guard uses `name.lower()` as key. Two items with identical names would be aggregated together (unlikely in practice, but worth noting).

success_rate.backend: 100% (53/53 tests: 25 returns flow + 18 exploratory + 10 FIFO regression)

seed_data_creation: Each pytest module seeds its own medicines (prefixed RTN_MED_* / EXP_*) with unique timestamps to avoid collisions with prior runs. No cleanup — historical data harmless.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Returns workflow is fully verified backend-side. LIFO deduct-on-confirm-receipt is stable; supplier credit is idempotent (ledger has exactly one entry per return_id, verified). If future changes touch batches.py::deduct_for_return, batches.py::consume_fifo, or accounting.py::apply_return_credit, re-run: `EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL=<url> pytest backend/tests/test_returns_flow.py backend/tests/test_returns_exploratory.py backend/tests/test_fifo_inventory.py -v`. The rename `restored_units` → `deducted_units` in the confirm-receipt response is now assumed by both test suites and the fix; do NOT revert.
rca_of_issue: N/A — the reported bug (batches.restore_batches originally ADDING stock back for purchase-returns) was already fixed by the main agent before this iteration. Verification confirms the fix is correct and consistent across all touched paths.
